newsitem.title: USA: No arrest seen imminent in Colorado girl's murder.
newsitem.headline: No arrest seen imminent in Colorado girl's murder.

text.p: Detectives investigating the death of 6-year-old JonBenet Ramsey said on Saturday they have interviewed dozens of people in Georgia who knew the young beauty pageant winner's family, but no arrests were imminent.

The body of the young girl, a former Little Miss Colorado, was discovered by her father in a basement room of the family's Boulder, Colorado, home on Dec. 26, about eight hours after the girl's mother said she found a ransom note demanding $118,000.

Boulder police Sgt. Larry Mason said detectives have interviewed about 30 family members and business associates of John and Patricia Ramsey, who lived in Georgia with their daughter until 1991. The Ramseys buried their daughter in Marietta, Georgia, on Tuesday.

"The family here has been more than helpful and we have gotten quite a bit" of information, Mason told reporters at a brief news conference. He said investigators would remain in Georgia for a few more days.
"We have not, nor do we anticipate, executing any search warrants or an arrest warrant while here," Mason said. "There are no arrests pending at this time and the investigation is ongoing."
Investigators announced a toll-free telephone number for information from the public that might help solve the unusual murder.
Both the Rocky Mountain News and The Denver Post reported on Saturday that the ransom note was written on paper from a pad found inside the house.
JonBenet's skull had been fractured by a blow to her head before a cord was twisted around her neck, the Rocky Mountain News also reported.
The newspaper, citing sources close to the investigation, said a security system at the Ramsey home in a posh Boulder neighbourhood was not operating when the girl was murdered on Christmas night.
Boulder authorities have remained tight-lipped about details of the murder, saying it was the best way to protect the integrity of the investigation.
The Ramseys returned to the Denver area from Georgia on Friday, but their whereabouts remain unknown. Boulder police were attempting to set up a formal interview with the couple, a spokeswoman said.
Yellow tape remained posted outside the Tudor-style 15-room Ramsey home, but local police were expected to wrap up their on-site work on Saturday.
